title: A signal in the water
hook: Movement can leave a trace after its source has passed.

knows: Animals have body structures and life histories.
doesNotKnow: Connect water movement with seal whisker sensing.

misconception: A familiar animal feature always has the first explanation that comes to mind.
objective: Connect water movement with seal whisker sensing.

claims.text: A seal’s whiskers can detect which kind of cue from a nearby swimming animal? The schematic connects a fish’s moving wake to whiskers at the seal’s muzzle. Seals can use whiskers to detect water movement; the drawing does not show a measured track or establish what a seal knows about a particular fish.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: Dehnhardt et al., Hydrodynamic Trail-Following in Harbor Seals, Science (2001), https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1060514

claims.text: The diagram and its labels are schematic, not to scale and not an observation. Seal and fish · schematic
A fish passes through dark water, leaving a small moving wake. Which seal structure could sense that water motion? Seal whiskers can respond to water movement.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: Dehnhardt et al., Hydrodynamic Trail-Following in Harbor Seals, Science (2001), https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1060514

recall.question: A fish passes through dark water, leaving a small moving wake. Which seal structure could sense that water motion?
recall.why: Seal whiskers can respond to water movement.
